name: Honda
overview: Celebrated for Formula 1-derived VTEC engine engineering, high-revving sports icons like the NSX, S2000, and Type R, and family benchmarks like CR-V and Civic.
australian_history:
Honda's automotive presence in Australia began in 1969 when Honda Australia Pty Ltd was established in Melbourne by Colin Campbell. Early imports included the air-cooled Honda Scamp (N360/N600) and the technically advanced 1300 Coupe.

The pivotal breakthrough arrived in 1973 with the first-generation Civic. Featuring a transverse engine, independent suspension, and the low-emission CVCC clean-burn engine, the Civic was perfectly timed for the 1973 oil crisis and won acclaim for space efficiency. In 1977, the larger Accord arrived, winning the 1977 Wheels Car of the Year award. The sleek Prelude coupe followed in 1979, becoming an aspirational status symbol for young Australian urban professionals.

In 1991, Honda shook the global exotic car hierarchy with the NSX (New Sportscar eXperimental). Featuring an all-aluminium monocoque, VTEC mid-engine V6, and chassis dynamics honed at Suzuka by Formula 1 champion Ayrton Senna, the NSX challenged Ferrari in Australian showroom prestige. In 1997, Honda launched the CR-V, sparking the Australian lifestyle compact SUV revolution. The 1999 S2000 roadster pushed naturally aspirated engine engineering to 9,000 rpm with 177kW from 2.0 litres.

In 2003, the European-specification Accord Euro (CL9) won the Wheels Car of the Year award, celebrated for its razor-sharp double-wishbone chassis and slick 6-speed manual gearbox. The Jazz city car introduced clever 'Magic Seats', while Type R variants of the Integra and Civic became Australian track-day royalty. In 2021, Honda Australia transitioned from a franchised dealer model to a national agency model with unified, non-negotiable pricing. Today, Honda's Australian range focuses on Civic (including the FL5 Type R), ZR-V, CR-V, and Accord e:HEV hybrid technology.

models_catalog.name: Civic
models_catalog.overview: Honda's enduring global icon, sold in Australia across eleven generations and home to the revered Civic Type R.

generations.summary: 1.2L EB1 and 1.5L CVCC engines, independent strut suspension, 1970s economy champion.
1.3L, 1.5L EW engines; 3rd-gen introduced flush aero styling and tall-roof Shuttle wagon.
Double-wishbone suspension front and rear, 1.5L D15 and 1.6L D16 DOHC engines.
Iconic split-tailgate hatch, 1.5L and 1.6L VTEC (VTi 96kW); GL, Breeze, VTi.
1.6L D16 and 1.6L B16A2 DOHC VTEC 118kW (VTI-R); CXi, GLi, VTi, VTi-R.
Dashboard-mounted gearshift, MacPherson front suspension, 1.7L D17 engine.
Two-tier digital instrument dash, 1.8L and 2.0L; UK-built FN2 Type R 2.0L K20Z4 148kW.
1.8L and 2.0L i-VTEC, VTi, VTi-L, VTi-S, Sport.
1.5L Turbo VTEC (127kW) and FK8 Type R with 2.0L Turbo K20C1 (228kW/400Nm).
Premium cabin, e:HEV hybrid powertrain and world-class FL5 Civic Type R 2.0L Turbo 235kW.

models_catalog.name: Accord Euro
models_catalog.overview: European-engineered sports sedan celebrated for benchmark double-wishbone chassis and tactile 6-speed manual; Wheels COTY 2003.

generations.summary: 2.4L K24A3 i-VTEC engine 140kW, 6-speed manual or 5-speed auto, Wheels COTY 2003.
Wider track, 2.4L K24Z3 148kW, standard/Luxury/Luxury Navi grades; final European Accord.

models_catalog.name: CR-V
models_catalog.overview: The vehicle that ignited Australia's lifestyle compact SUV revolution, complete with an in-floor picnic table in early models.

generations.summary: 2.0L B20B/B20Z engine, Real Time 4WD, flat cabin floor, folding picnic table in boot.
2.4L K24A1 i-VTEC engine 118kW, increased cargo space, dash-mounted handbrake.
Lower center of gravity, tailgate opening upward instead of outward, 2.4L K24Z 125kW.
Offered in 2WD and AWD, 2.0L and 2.4L petrol, plus 1.6L/2.2L i-DTEC diesel.
1.5L VTEC Turbo (140kW), available 7 seats, Honda Sensing safety suite.
1.5L Turbo petrol and 2.0L two-motor e:HEV hybrid; VTi X, VTi L, e:HEV RS.

models_catalog.name: S2000
models_catalog.overview: Pure naturally aspirated roadster celebrating Honda's 50th anniversary, featuring the F20C engine revving to 9,000 rpm.

generations.summary: 2.0L F20C DOHC VTEC producing 177kW at 8,300rpm, 50:50 weight distribution, X-bone frame.

models_catalog.name: NSX
models_catalog.overview: Mid-engine supercar that reset exotic car engineering standards with Ayrton Senna chassis development.

generations.summary: All-aluminum monocoque, 3.0L C30A (201kW) then 3.2L C32B (206kW) VTEC V6, 6-speed manual.
3.5L Twin-Turbo V6 with three electric motors (Sport Hybrid SH-AWD) generating 427kW.

models_catalog.name: Jazz
models_catalog.overview: Masterclass in interior packaging, renowned for its Magic Seats that allowed tall objects or flat camping beds inside a micro footprint.

generations.summary: Center-mounted fuel tank, Magic Seats, 1.3L i-DSI and 1.5L VTEC engines; GLi, VTi, VTi-S.
Expanded cabin, 1.3L and 1.5L i-VTEC, 5-speed auto/manual, introduced Jazz Hybrid in 2013.
1.5L direct-injected L15B engine 88kW, CVT automatic, final Jazz model sold in Australia.
